title: I built a tiny pixel café that lives in an iPhone widget, in about a week with Claude Code
author: s1ntez_ua
selftext:
I’ve been in programming and web design for quite a long time, mostly working with JS and building web apps, but I’ve always been interested in iOS development — and *boy oh boy*, Claude makes development so much easier and more fun.

I wanted to create something cozy, maybe in a niche category, and came up with the idea of a tiny café running as a widget on my phone’s Home Screen. After a few days of research together with Claude, we validated that the idea should work. Then, after around a week of heavy prompting, testing, playing around and having a lot of fun, the idea became an actual working product.

  
The main idea is more like Tamagotchi, but as a Cafe :) You don't need to rush anything, the customers come around during their day, enjoy a coup of Joe and pay with coins, which you can use to add additional decor to your Cafe.

By design, iOS doesn’t allow animations in widgets, but Claude found a clever way around it: an animated font that simulates slow-paced animation, so the widgets even feel a little alive. Then came the idea to extend the full view of the Cafe in the app with weather effects, which led to a lighting system with shadows, glow and some nice cozy effects.

The whole time I was driving Opus 5.5, and I’m really amazed by this model: music, animations, game ideas, validation and research, basically anything is possible now (at least for such projects).

I hope you’ll check out the game and have a good time with it!

**Kissa: Pixel Café** on the App Store: [https://apps.apple.com/app/id6823629734](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6823629734)

![img](97gkch7veowh1 "Where it started and where it is now: the first widget on 15 Oct was a 48-pixel room. Later that evening it became a 96-pixel street-front café, and today it’s 128 pixels, with light, shadows and weather.")
